text:
Maria (Support): Hey @Ryan, ACME reports a sudden spike of 502s and TLS handshake timeouts to our hosted inference endpoint since ~09:03 UTC. Customer says errors happen from a subset of their end-users (multiple ISPs). I collected sample logs.
Ryan (SRE): thanks — any immediate headers or error messages? TLS handshake timeout vs 'upstream reset'? can you paste a curl or svc log
Maria (Support): From ACME app logs: `grpc: failed to connect: timeout after 10s (handshake)` and our edge logs show `UPSTREAM_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT` and `TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` intermixed. sample client IPs: 3.44.12.9, 54.183.2.14 (different ISPs)
Dan (Oncall): I see increased TCP connection attempts that don't complete the TLS handshake on a subset of frontends. Tracing shows these requests were routed through resolver pool P3 and hit a few regions then failed.
Shreya (Net Eng): Can you run `dig +short A hosted.acme.redwood.ai @<customer-resolver>` from one of their failing hosts and a passing host? When resolvers return different CNAME/A sets across ISPs, SNI+cert mapping can break during a cert rotation.
Maria (Support): ACME ran dig for us. Failing client (ISP A):
```
$ dig +short hosted.acme.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
104.45.12.8
```
Passing client (ISP B):
```
$ dig +short hosted.acme.redwood.ai @9.9.9.9
52.88.33.7
```
Same CNAME expected, but A records differ — looks like multi-path DNS returning different edge pools.
Acme SRE (customer): We saw this hit first around 09:03 after we rotated our clients' cert pinning for a short window. We rolled back but some users still hit 502s.
Ryan (SRE): That fits a windowed mismatch: if our certs were rotating and DNS multipath sends clients to a pool with old certs, clients that validate SNI+cert pinning will time out or close. Need to confirm cert rotation windows and resolver behavior.
Dan (Oncall): I pulled edge cert rotation timeline: rotation started 09:01 UTC, finalization at 09:04 UTC. TTL on the customer-facing CNAME is 300s. During rotation, some resolvers still cached old IPs for a bit and hit a pool with previous cert state.
Shreya (Net Eng): Next steps to reproduce:
- from failing IP: `curl -v --resolve hosted.acme.redwood.ai:443:104.45.12.8 https://hosted.acme.redwood.ai/health` (observe TLS handshake failure or cert mismatch)
- run `tcpdump -n -s 0 -w /tmp/trace.pcap port 443 and host <edge-ip>` to capture SYN/ACK/TLS ClientHello
Also check EDNS0 behaviour; some ISPs truncate and fallback to TCP DNS which can flip answers.
Maria (Support): ACME provided a tcpdump snippet showing SYN/ACK but no ServerHello for some sessions. They also captured `ClientHello: SNI=hosted.acme.redwood.ai` then connection reset.
Ryan (SRE): temp mitigation options:
- Increase client connect timeout to 20s to tolerate brief rotation delays (not ideal but reduces churn)
- Ask ACME to lower their DNS TTL during rotations (e.g., 60s) for upcoming planned rotations
- Route traffic away from the small resolver pool (P3) by adjusting smart-routing policy for 30m
- Add a brief canary overlap in cert rotation so both certs accepted on edge during rollouts
Shreya (Net Eng): Also suggest forcing IPv4 on affected clients as a test: some IPv6 paths were showing packet loss in our edges' metrics. `curl -4` can be a quick repro.
Acme SRE (customer): We can temporarily set TTL=60 and flush our internal caches. Also can you confirm which edge IPs to avoid so we can map them in debug logs?
Dan (Oncall): I'll export the list of IPs assigned to resolver pool P3 and share. For now we put an emergency routing rule to deprioritize P3 for ACME's route ID at 09:18 UTC. Monitoring — errors started to drop after 09:22 UTC.
ops-bot: Incident note created: INCIDENT-2026-3078129999 - partial TLS handshake failures for ACME due to multi-resolver path during cert rotation. Owner: Ryan (SRE).
Maria (Support): ACME confirms user errors decreased after we deprioritized that pool and after they lowered TTL. They still ask for a root cause summary and permanent fix.
Ryan (SRE): Action items:
- Net to add overlap acceptance during cert rotations (Shreya)
- Routing: make resolver-path fallbacks faster and add health-check gating on cert presence (Dan)
- Support: send ACME postmortem with repro steps, mitigation, and suggested client-side TTL change (Maria)
Shreya (Net Eng): I'll open a runbook PR to include `verify cert chain post-rotation` and add a pre-rotation probe that validates certs from multiple public resolvers.
Maria (Support): I'll draft the customer note w/ curl/dig repro, tcpdump hints, and suggested mitigations. Thanks all :thumbsup:
